routes.route: Plymouth City Council council land and property
routes.outcome: Official council page found in first-party discovery. It states the council only holds records of council-owned land and directs privately owned land enquiries to HM Land Registry; it links an indicative council-owned-land map but not a cadastral parcel API. Direct command-line GET returned HTTP 403, so the page text is recorded from the first-party search result only.
routes.scope: Local council land/property context, not proof of citywide cadastral coverage.

routes.route: Plymouth City Council local land charges
routes.outcome: Official council procedure found. It says local land charges are dealt with by HM Land Registry and identifies the council as Commons Registration Authority for register-of-common-land, register-map and related documents. Direct command-line GET returned HTTP 403, so no interactive council map or geometry was extracted.
routes.scope: Local procedure/custodian evidence; not a downloadable parcel layer.

routes.route: HM Land Registry INSPIRE dataset guidance
routes.outcome: First-party guidance found. INSPIRE Index Polygons are indicative positions/extents of registered freehold property in England and Wales, each with a unique Land Registry-INSPIRE ID; data is published as GML and is not a title plan.
routes.scope: National source; not Plymouth-specific local custodianship.

routes.route: HM Land Registry current INSPIRE download page
routes.outcome: HTTP 302/self-redirect behavior. The current page was discoverable and search results listed Plymouth City Council as a local-authority download, but the anonymous request looped at the service boundary and no GML file was downloaded. No login or credentials were attempted.
routes.scope: Download availability indicated by first-party page, but no response artifact was used.

routes.route: HM Land Registry INSPIRE WMS GetCapabilities
routes.outcome: HTTP 200 XML metadata. Layer inspire:CP.CadastralParcel is polygonal, covers Great Britain, and advertises EPSG:27700 and CRS:84. The service was accessed anonymously with normal TLS verification.

routes.route: HM Land Registry WMS GetFeatureInfo at exact WUP point
routes.outcome: HTTP response was a LayerNotQueryable service exception: the advertised WMS layer is not queryable through GetFeatureInfo. No parcel ID or geometry was obtained. This is a service limitation, not evidence of absence at the point or citywide.
routes.scope: Exact-point bounded probe only; no hit/miss conclusion.

routes.outcome: A diagnostic status check was accidentally run once with curl -k. Its 403 results were discarded and were not used as evidence; all retained HTTPS evidence uses normal TLS verification.
routes.scope: Discarded diagnostic only; no source conclusion depends on it.

schemaAndCrs.geometryType: polygon according to WMS layer title/schema context
schemaAndCrs.serviceCrs: EPSG:27700 (British National Grid); CRS:84 also advertised
schemaAndCrs.nativeIdentity: Land Registry-INSPIRE ID (documented by HMLR guidance), not observed in a feature response

fieldMapping.Land Registry-INSPIRE ID: stable native polygon identity documented by HMLR; not retained because no feature response was obtained

sample.reason: No safe bounded anonymous ID+geometry response was returned; no sample GeoJSON was written.

uncertaintyAndLimits: The WUP point is preserved exactly in latitude/longitude order and was not shifted to force a hit.
The exact-point WMS request was not queryable; this is not evidence of citywide absence.
The download page redirected in a loop, so current Plymouth GML was not downloaded or inspected.
Council pages provide local land-charges/register-map procedure evidence, but no public local parcel geometry service was found.
INSPIRE polygons show indicative registered freehold property extents and are not title plans; coverage excludes some tenures and does not establish legal boundary extent.
No owner, address, contact, titleholder, tax/account, or other unsafe fields were requested or retained.

No login, credentials, private token, CAPTCHA/Cloudflare bypass, or intentional source-specific TLS exception was used. One accidental curl -k diagnostic was discarded and is explicitly recorded above.
